$comment: Share images and social posts. Layouts and opening copy follow the brand's image tool in agd-playground (src/components/opencommerce-og/draw.ts and Editor.tsx, routes opencommerce-og-image-playground and opencommerce-social-post). The four layouts there are hero, window, closing and cards; the CLI keeps its earlier five (headline, lead, frame, quote, announcement) beside them. Sizes are the tool's six plus the social set. Colors, radii, shadows, faces, tracking and line heights come from brand/tokens.css; where the tool's literals disagree, the token wins (see notes). Pixel sizes are the tool's, in the 1200x630 preview's pixels, grown with the image's area (unit k).

notes: Line heights: the tool sets headlines at 1.04 and the line under them at 1.5; the tokens say --ds-leading-heading 1.02 and --ds-leading-lead 1.55, and the CLI uses the tokens.

Window drop: the tool's canvas shadow is rgba(23,24,24,0.22) with a 32px blur and no spread; the CLI draws --ds-shadow-card (a hairline drop and 0 12px 32px -20px at 22 percent), so the drop is tighter than the tool's.
Headline weight: the tool sets the display face at 500; the CLI outlines the bundled substitute (TeX Gyre Heros, one weight), since Neue Haas Grotesk Display is not licensed to ship.
Attribution chip: the tool draws Agentcard's own lockup after 'Product by'. That lockup is not a file in brand/logo, so the CLI typesets the maker's name in the display face instead.
Merchants: the tool can fill the window with sixteen store logos (public/opencommerce-og). Those are third-party marks and are not shipped; the window takes code or your own --image.
Lockup: the tool follows the name with 'Product by' and Agentcard's lockup; the CLI uses brand/logo/lockup.svg (the name and 'by Agentcard').
Hero without room for its window: the tool leaves the words at the top; the CLI centers them, as it does when the window is turned off.
The window arrow is typed in the platform mono; the bundled mono has no such glyph, so it is drawn from Inter.
Code in a narrow window: the tool lets long lines run past the window's edge (hero on a tall image); the CLI shrinks the code until its longest line fits.
